Chapter 1: The Search for What Makes Us Come Alive.
Have you ever found yourself wondering, "Is this really all there is?" Maybe it's a quiet feeling during your morning commute, or a restlessness that lingers, no matter how much you try to brush it aside. You're definitely not alone. All around us, there are people who sense they're meant for something more—something they can't quite put their finger on.
That search for "something more"—that's really the heart of finding your Element. It's that magical spot where what you're naturally good at meets what you love most.
For a lot of us, the story actually begins in childhood. Remember when the world felt wide open and anything seemed possible? Maybe you spent hours lost in drawing, building, or making music. Not because you had to, but because it just felt right. But as we get older, life piles on its demands. School, family expectations, society—they all start to nudge us toward what’s considered “practical.” That kid who built amazing forts? Suddenly, they're told to focus on something more sensible. The dreamer? Asked to be realistic.
Take the story of one woman who grew up in a home where grades and academic success were everything. She loved to draw, filling notebook after notebook with sketches. But her parents, worried about her future, steered her away from art. She listened, excelled in school, and landed a solid job in finance. On the outside, she looked like a success story. But inside, she felt empty. Years later, after a chance meeting with an old friend who remembered her childhood artwork, she picked up a pencil again. And in that moment, she felt a spark she hadn’t felt in ages. She finally realized that true fulfillment comes from reconnecting with what brings you alive—not ticking off boxes on someone else’s checklist.
This story isn’t rare. So many people drift into careers or daily routines that seem sensible, only to end up feeling restless, even disengaged. The world is full of folks who are perfectly competent, yet uninspired—productive, but not truly fulfilled. What's missing? Most of the time, it’s the Element—that special mix of what you’re naturally good at and what you love doing.
Most don’t even notice this gap until something shakes up their routine. Maybe it's losing a job, a health scare, or simply realizing that time is slipping by and dreams are gathering dust. Suddenly, the question changes. Instead of “What should I do?” it becomes, “What do I really want to do?” The answer isn’t always clear—but chances are, you won’t find it by following someone else’s script.
Here's something important to remember: The search for your Element isn’t about chasing fame or making a fortune. It’s about finding that place where your abilities and your passion overlap, where work starts to feel less like a chore and more like an expression of who you are. For some, it’s rediscovering a childhood hobby. For others, it means trying out something new that’s always been in the back of their mind.
Think of the man who spent decades in a corporate job, only to find his Element in woodworking after retirement. He’d always enjoyed working with his hands, but never saw it as a “real” pursuit. Building furniture in his garage, he found a sense of satisfaction that had eluded him for years. Soon, friends and neighbors were asking for pieces, and he was busier—and happier—than ever.
Stories like his reveal something simple but powerful: Everyone has an Element. Not everyone finds it, but it’s there. The journey takes curiosity, a bit of courage, and sometimes the willingness to challenge what others expect of you. It’s not about ignoring your responsibilities, but about honoring the parts of yourself that make you feel most alive.
When people operate from their Element, something amazing happens. They bring energy, creativity, and real purpose to whatever they do. The trick is recognizing that the path isn’t always straight. The clues to our true passions are often hidden in the things we do when no one’s watching.
So, if you’re feeling that itch—that sense there’s something more out there—maybe it’s time to start looking for your Element. Who knows? You just might discover what truly makes you come alive.
